_about: Look of every outdoor scene (scripts/world/day_night.gd): warm low sun against a cool blue ambient, soft shadows, filmic AgX tone, glow, distance haze plus light valley mist, and the screen effects each graphics preset turns on. Visual tuning only; no gameplay reads it.

sun._about: elevation: the sun's height is scaled by this (1 = the old high noon sun, lower = longer, warmer light). warmth: how far day sun colours are pulled towards warm_color.

ambient._about: A cool blue fill: sky_contribution < 1 mixes in color, so shadows read blue against the warm sun. min_energy: the floor for every play space — ambient never drops below it (times the mode's mood_scale, so a staged scene like the hub's door talk can still go darker on purpose). At night the sky is black, so the sky's share falls to night_sky_contribution and the colour turns to night_color (moonlit blue): the character's unlit side and the ground stay readable.

camera_fill._about: Night only: a weak cool shadowless light AT the camera with a short range, so the side of the character the camera sees (his back, away from a fire) and the ground before him are readable, while far walls keep the night. energy at full night, times mood_scale.

haze._about: Exponential distance fog (all presets) and the valley's height mist (fog_height).

volumetric._about: Volumetric fog (medium: coarse and short; high: finer, longer, lit by SDFGI). density is thin on purpose: a light valley mist, not a wall.

sdfgi._about: SDFGI, only when Settings.global_illumination is on (experimental, off by default). Checked after the material fix: reading the sky still turns characters and trees chrome-white on the Intel UHD (its probes, not the materials), so it does not read the sky and two shadowless cool sky_fill lights stand in (energy = sky_fill x the hour's ambient). Without GI they are off: the sky ambient does their job.

presets._about: What each graphics preset (Settings.quality) turns on. SDFGI is not a preset: it is the separate, experimental Settings.global_illumination (off by default). ssao_quality (very_low | low | medium | high | ultra) and ssao_half (half resolution): Medium runs SSAO at its cheapest (docs/PERF_PROFILE.md: it was 4-10 ms of the frame on the Intel UHD). terrain: the ground shader's level (full | lean | lightweight, scripts/world/terrain_setup.gd apply_detail). All presets stay on full until the owner picks: lightweight saves about 3.7 ms at the valley's start and 2.6 ms in Kürköy at Medium on the Intel UHD and looks the same on flat ground, but stretches textures on steep slopes.

benchmark._about: First time in a gameplay scene (scripts/systems/benchmark.gd). It waits for READY — the scene's _begin has run, the streamer has nothing pending, and ready_frames more frames were drawn (at most ready_cap seconds) — then times every frame for `seconds` at Medium with vsync off. The MEDIAN decides: >= high_fps High (never on an integrated GPU), >= medium_fps Medium, <= low_fps Low; between low_fps and medium_fps (the dead zone) it runs at Medium and saves only when the next launch's measurement agrees. Nothing measured keeps Medium. The 1% low is logged; the notice stays notice_seconds. THRESHOLDS: measured at the valley's start spot, where Kürköy runs at about 74% of that frame rate at Medium (docs/PERF_PROFILE.md); they must be recalibrated after art part 2.

shadows._about: min_caster_size: a model whose largest side is under this many metres never casts a shadow (small props; grass never does). Applied where models are placed: scripts/world/visuals.gd no_small_shadows.
